title: A day of resolve
hook: do the thing you've been putting off
tomorrow: why picture a mother's love for one child to mean love for all?

segments.voice: Yesterday, King Nemi came back from seeing heaven and hell and resolved to govern well. He resolved. A resolve is a promise. Today asks when it starts.

Every to-do list has one line that never gets crossed off. Call the dentist. Write the email. Every morning it slides to tomorrow. Here's a scene about tomorrow. A grove near Kusinara, between two sala trees. The Buddha is lying on his right side, and he is dying. The monks have gathered close. He asks them whether anyone still has a doubt, a question they've been meaning to ask. Ask now, he says, so you won't be sorry later that your teacher was right here and you said nothing. Nobody speaks. Then he says the last thing he'll ever say. What would anyone spend their last words on?
screen: `THE LINE THAT NEVER GETS CROSSED OFF.` → `TWO SALA TREES, KUSINARA.` → `ASK NOW, HE SAYS.` → `HIS LAST WORDS.`

segments.voice: Here they are, in Rhys Davids' old translation: "Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!" Two sentences, and they lean on each other. The first is the reason. The second is the job. Everything put together comes apart: the body, the plan, the free afternoon. So the work can't wait for a better week. The Pali word under diligence is appamada: heedfulness, not letting things slide. Not panic, and not a grind. Just not sleeping through it. A sutta in the Majjhima Nikaya says it even more plainly: do today's work with energy, because who knows, death may come tomorrow, and there's no bargain to strike with it. That line isn't there to frighten anyone. It's there to shrink the gap between knowing and doing. And look at the scene again. Before his last words, he asked for questions. He gave everyone one more chance to say the thing they'd been putting off saying. So a day of resolve isn't a day of doing everything. It's a day of doing the one thing. The email. The apology. The first page. Yesterday, resolve lived in a heart. Today it gets a date.
screen: `THE REASON: THINGS COME APART.` · `THE JOB: APPAMADA, HEEDFULNESS.` · `DO TODAY'S WORK TODAY.` · `HE ASKED FOR QUESTIONS FIRST.` · then, large: `TODAY, NOT SOMEDAY.`

segments.voice: Sit easy and let the one thing you've been putting off come to mind. Don't solve it. Shrink it: find the very first move, small enough to take five minutes, and see yourself making it right after this sit.
A day of resolve: the day a promise gets a date, and the date is today. Appamada, heedfulness, is what keeps it.
Keep this one: today, not someday, the job the last words gave. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: the frame shop's help-wanted sign is still up. i keep telling myself i'll ask next week.
options: Ask today. Next week keeps moving; the first move is just walking in.
Wait until you feel ready. Resolve means holding out for the right moment.
Deciding is the resolve. You've decided, so going later still counts.
chat.meaning: The Buddha's last words tie the reason to the job: things change, so don't let it slide. A small move today beats a perfect someday.
